deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck's 1974 'topologie modérée' notes work in a tame ('par morceaux') category of spaces, such as PL, semi-analytic or semi-algebraic. An admissible partition of X is a finite partition into connected 'feuilles' (leaves, i.e. strata). Each leaf is a manifold, and 'équisingularité' holds: the partition is locally trivial along each leaf. A privileged partition is an admissible one satisfying further conditions. The 'canonical' one is the coarsest. Conjecture 2 on the previous page asks for the following: for a finite poset I and an I-diagram of spaces with proper maps, privileged partitions compatible with the diagram exist, and there is a coarsest one.

(1) End of the Remark: let f: X -> Y be proper, with compatible admissible partitions, and let F be a leaf of X with f(F) contained in a leaf S of Y. Then f(F) = S.
- Openness: by equisingularity, f restricted to F (or to F meeting f^{-1}(S)) is open in S.
- Closedness: by properness, f of the closure of F meeting f^{-1}(S) is closed in S. Its difference with f(F) consists of images of boundary leaves F_i lying in closure(F) and in f^{-1}(S). These images are again open by equisingularity, so f(F) is clopen in S.
- Since S is connected, f(F) = S.
Moreover F, being locally trivial over the open set f(F), is a locally trivial fibration over all of S. Better: f^{-1}(S) with its induced partition is a locally trivial stratified fibration over S. Since F and S are manifolds, Grothendieck concludes that the fibres of F -> S are manifolds.

(2) Conjectural top-down construction of the canonical privileged partition of a proper map f: X -> Y, with Y compact. The page refers to an earlier conjectural description, for a single space, via 'immobile points' in connection with A'Campo.
- Let U be the largest open subset of Y that is nonsingular and over which X|U -> U is locally trivial.
- One must prove that Y' = Y - U is a rare tame subspace, so dim Y' < dim Y. This is a generic triviality statement.
- The connected components of U are the open top-dimensional leaves of Y.
- Over them, the leaves of X are those of the intrinsic canonical partition of V = X|U. Locally this is U times a canonical leaf of a fibre.
- Then recurse on X' -> Y'. The next page notes that X' must carry the traces Phi_i (closure of F_i over Y') of the leaves above. Hence the correct inductive statement involves spaces equipped with a finite family of closed subspaces. This reduces everything to the case of a single space with marked closed subsets, to be modelled on the A'Campo construction.

In modern terms this is a sketch of the existence of a canonical (coarsest) topologically locally trivial stratification of a proper tame map, compatible with given closed subsets. It is built by peeling off the generic-triviality locus and inducting on dim Y.
errors: The written justification of closedness is muddled. 'S - f(F) is a union of images of leaves contained in closure(F) and f^{-1}(S)' is not literally right. What is meant is that f(closure(F) meeting f^{-1}(S)) is closed and equals f(F) together with the open images of boundary leaves. The cleanest proof is simply that local triviality of the partition of f^{-1}(S) over the connected S makes 'the fibre meets F' a locally constant condition.

'Since F and S are manifolds, the fibres of F over S are manifolds' needs qualification. With only topological local triviality it is false, even for polyhedral/semi-algebraic fibres. Example: Phi = cone on the Poincaré homology sphere P gives Phi x R^2 = c(P * S^1) = c(Sigma^2 P), which is homeomorphic to R^5 by Cannon-Edwards, yet Phi is not a manifold. It holds if trivializations are PL and 'variété' means PL manifold, since links of a product are suspensions of links. So the claim depends on the precise tame category and on what 'variété' means. Grothendieck's trailing '...' may signal awareness.

Two points in the top-down construction are left unproved. The first is that Y - U is rare; this is a generic triviality theorem, later proved by Varchenko and by Hardt. The second is that the recursively obtained partition actually satisfies the frontier/closure conditions and is the coarsest. The second is genuinely non-trivial, since the strata over Y' are forced to refine by the traces Phi_i. Grothendieck flags this in footnote 6 of the next page.

ideas.what: For proper compatible admissible partitions, a leaf mapping into a leaf maps onto it, and the preimage of a leaf is a locally trivial stratified fibration over it
ideas.modern_name: Stratified submersion / Thom's first isotopy lemma consequence for proper stratified maps

ideas.what: Canonical coarsest partition of a space characterized intrinsically (via 'immobile points')
ideas.usually_credited_to: Akin (1969) for polyhedra; Sullivan; King (1985) and Habegger-Saper in intersection homology
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5-6 discusses tame topology and stratifications in general terms

ideas.what: Largest nonsingular open set over which the map is locally trivial has rare complement
ideas.usually_credited_to: Varchenko (1972, algebraic), Hardt (1980, semi-algebraic/subanalytic), later o-minimal versions (van den Dries)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions a 'dévissage' theory of tame maps, without this statement explicitly

ideas.what: Top-down recursive construction of the canonical stratification of a proper map, requiring the inductive hypothesis to include a finite family of marked closed subspaces
ideas.modern_name: Canonical/minimal stratification of maps compatible with given subsets (Hardt-style induction)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hardt (1980) for existence; minimal stratification questions by Mather, Teissier (Whitney case), du Plessis-Wall

missed.claim: Conjecture: every proper tame map (indeed every finite diagram of proper maps), with given closed subsets, has a canonical coarsest topologically locally trivial ('privileged') stratification. It is constructed top-down from the maximal locus of local triviality. Existence of some such stratification is now standard (Hardt, o-minimal triviality). The existence of a canonical coarsest one for maps and diagrams, with frontier condition, is to my knowledge not a standard theorem.
missed.quote: Considérons le plus grand ouvert U de Y tel que 1°) U est non singulier, 2°) X|U → U est un fibré loc. trivial. Il faut prouver que Y − U = Y' est un sous-espace ... rare
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Canonical stratifications of maps would give functorial constructible-sheaf and intersection-homology data for maps. The problem of a coarsest topological stratification of maps (as opposed to Whitney or a_f stratifications, which can fail) is still discussed in the o-minimal and singularity literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page sketches, in 1974, the generic-triviality-plus-recursion strategy for canonical stratifications of proper tame maps. This anticipates Hardt's 1980 theorem and later work on intrinsic stratifications. Grothendieck also sees that marked closed subsets must be carried through the induction. These are interesting historical precursors, but the content is conjectural and mostly standard in spirit today.
transcription_corrections: The script letter written for the target leaf is the same symbol throughout (rendered 𝔏/𝒮 in the transcriptions). On the previous page it was transcribed as $\mathcal{L}$ and here as $\mathcal{S}$; they denote the same leaf of Y.
The insertion '(⊂ F̄ ∩ f^{-1}(𝒮))' is written above the line after 'feuilles', apparently '(c F̄ ∩ f^{-1}(S))'. Its 'F_i' reading is plausible.
'Mieux, f^{-1}(𝒮) [est fibré avec] ✓ partition induite': the inserted text above the check mark is 'muni de la', consistent with the transcription.
